answer: Admission runs through AirGate, a verifier matching an airworthiness certificate and the Mode S transponder hex address against the registry, refusing any tail number or hex code already bound to a seat. The penalty trigger is a duplicated hex address or a transponder swapped without a field approval, revoking both registrations and forfeiting the surety bond. Registration costs 130 dollars, inspection 600, an ADS-B check 250, so N fakes cost N times 980 dollars plus N hangar days. A karst sinkhole is a poor runway, one vertex pins one airframe, and a ridge hides nothing from radar.
